narrative.title: Flipping Pallets a Truckload at a Time
narrative.scenario: A freight yard stacks outbound pallets in a single chain and a re-sequencer flips them in fixed batches of k so the oldest pallet of each batch ends up nearest the dock gate. If the chain ends with a partial batch — fewer than k pallets left — that leftover tail ships in its original order. The re-sequencer must confirm a full batch exists before flipping, then splice the flipped batch back onto the results of the remaining chain.
narrative.inputFormat: An array head of n node values and an integer k, the group size.
narrative.outputFormat: The values of the list after every complete group of k nodes is reversed and spliced back in order.

complexity.optimalSpace: O(1) iterative (O(n/k) recursion stack for the recursive form)

testCases.explanation: Two full batches flip to (2,1) and (4,3); the leftover single pallet 5 ships as-is.
The first batch of three flips to 3-2-1; the remaining pair 4-5 is a partial batch and stays untouched.

hintLevels: Level 1: This is ordinary list reversal, but gated — only start flipping once you know a full batch of k exists.
Level 2: Probe k nodes ahead first; if the probe falls off the end, return the chain untouched, otherwise reverse exactly k links.
Level 3: The original head of each batch becomes its tail after flipping — wire that tail's next to the already-processed remainder (recursion or a saved pointer) before moving to the next batch.
